summary: spec-judge round 1 stopped at the governance pre-flight: the producer declared 2 of the 7 bars the judge derived for artifact-type script, omitting the lifecycle, gate-validation, and all three resolved-actor spec bars
detail: Honest omission, not a skip-and-claim — but the omitted bars had genuinely not been read. Loading them found three real defects in the draft that the pre-flight would otherwise have let through to a content round: an uncovered CFG edge (project scope with no repo root), an unspecified continue-past-a-failing-engine decision, and a near-duplicate scenario kept without argument. All three fixed at the draft before re-dispatch.

summary: spec-judge round 2: oracle and architect pass, builder fails on three scenario-form defects — two Givens that are absence-defined or conjunctive, and a near-duplicate kept without argument
detail: All three substantiated against the rule rather than the instance. The two Givens matched suite-format's own worked bad example (absence has infinitely many fixtures; one condition per step) and were rewritten to name a present, buildable shape and split at the conjunction. The third was mis-aimed rather than duplicated: its row sits on the flag-check edge but its Then restated the sibling row's outcome, so it was re-aimed at the decision that edge actually owns — that with no scope flag the working directory is the project — and the map's argued-exception note now covers both kept rows. Swept for other instances of each rule across the suite; no further ones found.

summary: spec-judge round 3: one missed instance of round 2's own Given-conjunction rule, and one regression of round 2's remediation — the re-aimed scenario was justified on a decision the drawn CFG did not contain
detail: Provenance accounted for. Finding 2 names an artifact round 2's fix changed, so it is a regression, and it was re-planned rather than patched again. The wrong approach was carrying a decision in scenario-map prose instead of in the graph: round 2 answered a near-duplicate finding by asserting the scenario sat on a flag-check branch that was never drawn. New approach: every decision the surface trace names is drawn in the CFG. The graph now splits on where the run starts (corpus and a bare invocation from the working directory, --project from its argument) before the repo-root lookup, which also corrects an ordering error the old graph carried — it resolved the root above a directory it had not yet determined. The scenario moves to its own drawn edge in the UC2 group and stops being an argued exception. Swept the whole suite for both rules; one further conjunction found and split, no further undrawn decisions.

summary: spec-judge round 4: two new-territory builder findings — half the coverage guard was a dead edge, and the regression pin never named the literal flag its own discrimination argument depends on
detail: Neither is a regression: both name defects standing since the first draft, and both round-3 repairs were re-derived sound by the judge. Fixed at the rule. The coverage guard's definition carries two conditions that fail differently (a spec that does not classify is invisible to discovery; a spec that classifies but no project reaches is visible and still unchecked), so the CFG now draws them as two decisions rather than one, and the second gets its own scenario and its own end-to-end test. The regression pin's Given now names the literal flag, without which its stated discrimination against a vestigial special-case subject was unbuildable. Mutation-confirmed: removing the reachability half of the guard fails the new scenario's test and three standing unit tests. Grill has now exceeded the default 3-round cap; continued rather than auto-accepting, with the rationale reported to the owner.
